lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: The résumé lacks a summary or role-focused heading.
items.because: Readers have to infer the quantitative-research target from the experience section.

items.says: The strongest quantitative-research narrative starts too late.
items.because: The current bakery role can overshadow the statistical research applied to systematic finance.

items.says: The Northpeak bullets should put the clearest, best-validated research outcome first.
items.because: The strongest result is near the bottom, away from supporting validation evidence.

items.says: Consider shortening the bakery experience.
items.because: It takes attention away from the target field.

items.says: Clarify the scale or outcome of the weekly labour-budget responsibility.
items.because: It reads as a responsibility claim rather than a measurable result.

items.says: Use a consistent spelling convention for “labour.”
items.because: The U.S. location alongside that spelling may look inconsistent.

items.says: Clarify the basis of the 12%-to-7% unsold-bread comparison.
items.because: The comparison needs a clear basis.

items.says: Clarify whether the unsold-bread reduction was attributable to your changes.
items.because: The review says that attribution should be established.

items.says: Specify what the 35% risk-adjusted-returns improvement measures and its comparison point.
items.because: Without that context, the large improvement is difficult to interpret.

items.says: Give the test period and evaluation setting for the 35% improvement.
items.because: Without that context, the large improvement is difficult to interpret.

items.says: Explain the split design and how the embargo addressed leakage.
items.because: The validation claim supports the performance result.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to the feature store and what reuse in two later projects means.
items.because: That reuse is stronger evidence of impact than simply building the store.

items.says: Clarify whether the live allocation followed a research review.
items.because: The bullet describes a real decision-maker response without explaining that step.

items.says: Explain what “small” means for the live allocation if shareable.
items.because: The size of the allocation is unclear.

items.says: The allocation is mentioned without realized live-trading results.
items.because: The review calls the evidence of live-trading performance partial.

items.says: Reconsider reporting the best of 400 backtested Sharpes as the expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Treating a selected backtest result as a forward expectation raises overfitting and credibility concerns.

items.says: Distinguish parameter-selection data from an untouched evaluation set.
items.because: The expected-live-Sharpe claim sits beside claims of out-of-sample validation.

items.says: The 18-month order-book signal result also appears in the Kaggle project.
items.because: Presenting the same work twice can make it look like separate evidence.

items.says: Make the Sharpe comparison and testing period directly interpretable.
items.because: The review says the result needs a clearer comparison and test context.

items.says: Clarify the signal’s ownership and whether it is distinct from the Kaggle work.
items.because: The same signal and 18-month test may be reported in both places.

items.says: Verify or correct the claim that every Monte Carlo worker used the same random seed.
items.because: Identical seeds can produce duplicated or correlated streams, threatening valid replication.

items.says: Clarify your role in the variance-bound proof and the log-factor improvement.
items.because: The contribution and mathematical result should be explainable.

items.says: Prioritize research evidence over the teaching bullet if space is tight.
items.because: Teaching is less central to quantitative research.

items.says: Be able to substantiate and explain how the 3,000 downloads were measured.
items.because: The download count is a scale claim.

items.says: Clarify the baseline, evaluation period and forecasting setup for the 7% QLIKE improvement.
items.because: Those details are needed to interpret the result.

items.says: Clarify the testing procedure and how the crisis periods were identified.
items.because: Those details support the significance claim.

items.says: Emphasize the working paper’s status and seminar audience rather than its 12-page length.
items.because: The length is less persuasive than the work’s status and audience.

items.says: Add a specific result or contribution to the feature-engineering bullet.
items.because: It is generic compared with the other bullets and adds little beyond the project title.

items.says: Explain how the 0.02 validation-to-leaderboard gap was measured.
items.because: The review asks for the basis of that figure.

items.says: Explain why closing the gap improved confidence in model evaluation.
items.because: The benefit of the validation change needs to be clear.

items.says: The 18-month order-book signal result repeats the Northpeak internship result.
items.because: The same result should not be presented as distinct evidence.

items.says: Clarify the project’s timeline and your ownership of the order-book work.
items.because: It is unclear whether this was separate work, a precursor to the internship, or the same result.

items.says: Reassess whether Kafka belongs in Skills.
items.because: The résumé gives no supporting example of practical Kafka experience.

items.says: “Time-series econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: A typo in a skills keyword can hurt credibility and search matching.

items.says: Make the Skills section more informative about relevant methods and finance experience.
items.because: The section is brief, while the bullets carry much of that evidence.
